s:
Consider the following subjects with regard to Non- Cooperation Programme :
I. Boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth
II. Observance of strict non-violence
III. Retention of titles and honours without using them in public
IV. Establishment of Panchayats for settling disputes
How many of the above were parts of Non-Cooperation Programme?
x: The Non-Cooperation Programme was officially accepted by the Indian National Congress at the Calcutta Special Session in 1920 and then at the Nagpur Session in December 1920. The Non-Cooperation Programme accepted at the Nagpur Session included the following points – Renunciation of titles and honours; Boycott of law courts and foreign cloth; Establishment of panchayats to settle disputes; and the expectation that people strictly adhere to non-violence. The Congress and Gandhiji had called for a complete renunciation of the titles and honours given by the British government; there was no question of keeping them while merely avoiding their public use. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect. Hence, three out of the four statements are correct, and the correct option is (c).

x: In Sitaram Chaturvedi’s biography “Madan Mohan Malaviya (Builders of Modern India)”, published by the Publications Division, it is described that after the Chauri-Chaura incident 225 persons were arrested, and the Sessions Judge of Gorakhpur sentenced 170 of them to death. As no local lawyer was coming forward to defend them, all eyes turned to Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya when the cases came up for hearing before the Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court.
